Atkinson Index

Source: R/atkinson.R
atkinson.Rd

Computes the Atkinson inequality index.

atkinson(x, n = rep(1, length(x)), epsilon = 0.5, na.rm = FALSE)

Arguments

x

numeric vector of non-negative values, such as incomes

n

optional frequency weights. Each element of x is replicated n times.

epsilon

inequality aversion parameter \(\varepsilon\). Must be non-negative. The case epsilon = 1 is handled separately.

na.rm

logical. If TRUE, missing values are removed.

Value

numeric value of the Atkinson index in the interval [0, 1]

Details

The Atkinson index measures income inequality based on a social welfare function and includes an inequality aversion parameter \(\varepsilon >= 0\). Larger values of epsilon imply greater sensitivity to lower incomes.

The index is defined as

$$ A(\varepsilon) = 1 - \frac{\left( \frac{1}{n} \sum x_i^{1-\varepsilon} \right)^{1/(1-\varepsilon)}}{\bar{x}} $$

for \(\varepsilon \neq 1\). For \(\varepsilon = 1\),

$$ A(1) = 1 - \frac{\exp\left( \frac{1}{n} \sum \log x_i \right)}{\bar{x}} $$

If negative values or missing values (when na.rm = FALSE) are present, NA is returned.

References

Atkinson, A. B. (1970). On the measurement of inequality. Journal of Economic Theory.

See also

Other inequality: gini(), herfindahl(), lc(), rosenbluth(), simpson(), theil()
